Reviewer Comment: The manuscript covers too many areas and the central scientific claims are not validated with sufficient rigor.
Author Response: We will narrow the main contribution to embedded edge-NILM and smart-meter deployment, while presenting forecasting, web, mobile, payment, and harmonic functions as supporting system components.
Document Changes Made: Shorten generic web, mobile, payment, and smart-grid descriptions; sharpen the contribution statement; move nonessential implementation detail to supplementary material.

Reviewer Comment: The NILM evaluation protocol and the meaning of cross-dataset generalization are unclear.
Author Response: We will explicitly distinguish multi-dataset evaluation, unseen-household evaluation, temporal evaluation, and true source-to-target cross-dataset testing.
Document Changes Made: Add a complete experimental matrix showing training, validation, and test datasets and houses; revise cross-dataset claims unless new source-to-target experiments are added.

Reviewer Comment: Evaluation on separately trained models across SustDataED2, REFIT, and UK-DALE is multi-dataset validation, not necessarily cross-dataset generalization.
Author Response: We will revise the terminology to multi-dataset performance evaluation and unseen-household or temporal generalization where supported.
Document Changes Made: Replace unsupported cross-dataset generalization claims in the abstract, Introduction, Results, Discussion, captions, and Conclusion.

Reviewer Comment: The paper should add REFIT-to-UK-DALE, UK-DALE-to-REFIT, leave-one-house-out, unseen-house, zero-shot, and limited-adaptation evaluations.
Author Response: We will add the requested transfer experiments where feasible and clearly label zero-shot and adapted results. If experiments cannot be completed, the claims will be limited and the omission acknowledged.
Document Changes Made: Add source-to-target results, leave-one-house-out results, zero-shot results, and target-adaptation results with exact protocols, or revise the scope and limitations.

Reviewer Comment: The methodological novelty of EDTCN and the device-type-weighted focal loss is not isolated.
Author Response: We will provide controlled ablations to identify the contribution of architecture, loss design, quantization, and compiler optimization.
Document Changes Made: Add ablation tables using identical splits, training budgets, seeds, and metrics for standard TCN, residual/dilated variants, loss variants, FP32, INT8, and optimized deployment.

Reviewer Comment: The mathematical formulation of the device-type-weighted focal loss is incomplete, including weight derivation, class weights, focusing parameter, normalization, and threshold selection.
Author Response: We will define all loss terms, appliance weights, state thresholds, normalization, zero-state handling, and hyperparameter-selection procedures explicitly.
Document Changes Made: Rewrite the loss subsection and add a parameter table. Verify the claim that the relative-error focal term is bounded, or correct the formulation.

Reviewer Comment: It is unclear how focal loss, conventionally used for classification, is combined with appliance power regression.
Author Response: We will clearly separate the continuous regression model using the proposed weighted regression loss from the independent binary classification model using weighted BCE.
Document Changes Made: Clarify output heads, model instances, target construction, thresholds, and which model produces every reported MAE, precision, recall, and F1 value.

Reviewer Comment: A component-level statistical comparison is needed to demonstrate that EDTCN is more than a standard dilated TCN with empirical weighting.
Author Response: We will report repeated-run variation and statistical comparisons for each architectural and loss component.
Document Changes Made: Add confidence intervals or standard deviations across multiple seeds and appropriate paired tests across the controlled ablations.

Reviewer Comment: The real-time execution claim is unclear because inference takes approximately 111 seconds.
Author Response: We will distinguish computational throughput from end-to-end responsiveness and explain the relationship between window duration, buffering, inference, and output updates.
Document Changes Made: Report input-window duration, number of samples, acquisition rate, output interval, time to first prediction, buffering delay, and the source of the 111-second value. Correct inconsistent values in the text and tables.

Reviewer Comment: A 21-minute context window processed in 111 seconds may still introduce substantial output delay.
Author Response: We will moderate strict real-time claims and state that the current implementation demonstrates throughput suitable for periodic analytics, not necessarily rapid control or anomaly response.
Document Changes Made: Add a latency diagram and separate buffering, preprocessing, inference, postprocessing, and communication latency.

Reviewer Comment: CPU utilization approaches 100 percent, so concurrent metrology, FFT, display, tamper detection, communication, and storage must be evaluated.
Author Response: We will measure concurrent workloads and report whether the system meets its intended scheduling and responsiveness requirements.
Document Changes Made: Add workload-concurrency measurements, task priorities, scheduling policy, worst-case execution time, and any missed acquisition or communication deadlines.

Reviewer Comment: The Discussion should be more argumentative and explain why the tested results were achieved.
Author Response: We will reorganize the Discussion around mechanisms supported by the results rather than repeating numerical findings.
Document Changes Made: Explain the effects of sampling rate, appliance overlap, duty cycle, receptive field, loss weighting, quantization, and hardware constraints; connect each explanation to measured evidence.

Reviewer Comment: The literature review should include recent work on intelligent energy management, optimization-assisted forecasting, nonlinear dynamics, hybrid deep learning, and AI-based estimation.
Author Response: We will add the requested studies and explain their methodological relevance without implying direct application equivalence.
Document Changes Made: Expand the forecasting and intelligent-energy-management literature review and cite the four specified studies in the appropriate methodological context.

Reviewer Comment: Active-power reduction is reported inconsistently as 71.59 percent and 92.6 percent.
Author Response: We will recalculate every reduction using an explicitly named baseline and use consistent denominators.
Document Changes Made: Correct the abstract, Table 2, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Report current, voltage, power, and baseline for each percentage.

Reviewer Comment: Table 2 reports 695.68 mA at 5 V as 2.71 W, which is numerically inconsistent.
Author Response: We will recalculate all current-to-power conversions and verify the source measurements.
Document Changes Made: Correct Table 2 and all dependent reduction percentages; distinguish idle from active current and power.

Reviewer Comment: The abstract reports a 3���5 dollar cost while Table 2 reports a development-board price of approximately 16 do

Document Changes Made: Revise cost wording in the abstract and tables and provide a complete bill of materials.

Reviewer Comment: A complete bill of materials should be provided for the deployable meter.
Author Response: We will provide component, quantity, unit-cost, and cost-basis information for the complete meter.
Document Changes Made: Add a BOM covering the SoC or board, STPM33, sensors, display, storage, power supply, communications, PCB, enclosure, and assembly assumptions.

Reviewer Comment: The paper should report total system power, including processor, STPM33, display, analog front end, storage, communication, and power-supply losses.
Author Response: We will separate board-only measurements from complete-system measurements and report the total meter power under defined operating modes.
Document Changes Made: Add idle, metrology-only, NILM, display/network-active, and complete-system power measurements with instrument and uncertainty details.

Reviewer Comment: The manuscript should state whether the 0.513 W figure includes the TFT display and metrology components.
Author Response: We will state exactly which components are included in each reported power value.
Document Changes Made: Add an explicit measurement boundary and revise the 0.513 W claim if it represents only processor-board power.

Reviewer Comment: The phrase without FPU support should clarify whether software-emulated floating-point preprocessing occurs before INT8 inference.
Author Response: We will clarify that the processor has no hardware FPU and identify all software-emulated floating-point operations in preprocessing, runtime, and postprocessing.
Document Changes Made: Update the deployment subsection with compiler flags, data types, preprocessing arithmetic, and residual floating-point operations.

Reviewer Comment: The EDTCN architecture should be presented in a complete layer-by-layer table.
Author Response: We will provide the exact implemented architecture rather than only a conceptual diagram.
Document Changes Made: Add input and output sizes, channels, kernels, dilation, padding, residual paths, activations, parameters, and output dimensions for every layer.

Reviewer Comment: The receptive-field calculation resulting in 127 timesteps should be derived explicitly.
Author Response: We will recalculate the receptive field from the exact number of convolutions per block and correct the stated value if necessary.
Document Changes Made: Add the formula and intermediate values; reconcile the current 127 versus 129 inconsistency and verify the implementation.

Reviewer Comment: The mapping of 127 timesteps to 21 minutes depends on a 10-second sampling interval and must be stated clearly.
Author Response: We will state the sampling interval separately for each dataset and remove any time interpretation that does not match the actual preprocessing.
Document Changes Made: Correct the 1-Hz, 8-second, and 10-second statements and ensure receptive-field duration, input-window duration, and table captions agree.

Reviewer Comment: Dataset preprocessing needs details on missing values, resampling, normalization, synchronization, thresholds, activation filtering, periods, and voltage systems.
Author Response: We will document a dataset-specific preprocessing protocol with no ambiguity about training-only transformations.
Document Changes Made: Add a reproducibility table covering timestamps, missing values, resampling, scaling, appliance thresholds, activation filtering, split periods, and voltage-system handling.

Reviewer Comment: Evaluation should include normalized disaggregation error and signal aggregate error in addition to MAE and F1.
Author Response: We will add standard NILM metrics and define them mathematically.
Document Changes Made: Report SAE, normalized disaggregation error, energy estimation accuracy, MAE, RMSE, precision, recall, and F1 consistently across datasets and appliances.

Reviewer Comment: Results should be reported separately for each appliance rather than relying mainly on dataset-level averages.
Author Response: We will make per-appliance results central to the evaluation and distinguish macro averages from weighted averages.
Document Changes Made: Retain or expand complete per-appliance tables for every dataset and explain aggregation rules.

Reviewer Comment: The relatively low REFIT and UK-DALE F1 scores should be discussed critically.
Author Response: We will explicitly interpret F1 of 0.448 and 0.531 as mixed performance rather than uniformly strong state detection.
Document Changes Made: Revise the Results, Discussion, Abstract, and Conclusion to discuss failures, appliance overlap, low-power loads, false positives, and energy-error trade-offs.

Reviewer Comment: The claim of near-perfect state detection should be removed unless it applies to all relevant appliances.
Author Response: We will restrict the claim to the specific high-performing appliances and dataset where it is supported, or remove it.
Document Changes Made: Replace near-perfect and similar language with appliance-specific performance descriptions.

Reviewer Comment: The 30.6 percent precision problem needs its exact experimental setting and appliance distribution explained.
Author Response: We will identify the dataset, model type, threshold, appliance set, averaging method, and confusion counts behind the 30.6 percent value.
Document Changes Made: Add a metric-definition paragraph and report per-appliance precision, positive rates, threshold, and macro or micro averaging.

Reviewer Comment: The cloud LSTM forecasting module is weakly connected to the edge-NILM contribution.
Author Response: We will either shorten the forecasting module and present it as a supporting cloud service or justify its role in the complete NGSM architecture.
Document Changes Made: Clarify forecasting data split, horizon, baselines, deployment location, relationship to NILM, and failure behavior under network loss.

Reviewer Comment: A forecasting MAE of 12.70 W cannot be interpreted without scale, horizon, and baseline performance.
Author Response: We will report target-signal scale, forecast horizon, persistence or naive baseline, and normalized performance measures.
Document Changes Made: Revise the forecasting table and discussion with MAE, RMSE, MAPE, normalized error, horizon, and baseline comparisons.

Reviewer Comment: Cold-start adaptation and EWC are discussed, but the actual adaptation protocol is not fully described.
Author Response: We will provide the complete adaptation protocol or remove claims that imply the experiments implemented EWC or continual learning.
Document Changes Made: Specify updated parameters, target-data amount and labels, location of adaptation, optimizer, epochs, validation isolation, and zero-shot versus adapted results.

Reviewer Comment: The dishwasher MAE reduction from over 100 W to approximately 1 W after adaptation is unusually large and requires validation against leakage or overfitting.
Author Response: We will reproduce the result using a leakage-free protocol and report repeated runs, target-data size, and independent test performance.
Document Changes Made: Add adaptation curves, zero-shot baseline, held-out target test set, multiple houses or appliances, and an explanation of any unusually large improvement.

Reviewer Comment: Hardware comparison should use equivalent workloads and identical peripherals.
Author Response: We will distinguish platform-level benchmarking from processor-efficiency comparison and control peripherals and workload conditions where possible.
Document Changes Made: Add a controlled benchmark table with identical model, input, display, network, storage, and metrology conditions, or explicitly limit the comparison claim.

Reviewer Comment: Power measurement methodology should specify instrument, sampling interval, averaging period, uncertainty, voltage stability, and peripheral activity.
Author Response: We will document the measurement setup and uncertainty and state which peripherals and workloads were active.
Document Changes Made: Add a power-measurement subsection and update all hardware table notes.

Reviewer Comment: Thermal measurements should be included during sustained inference.
Author Response: We will measure temperature at startup and during sustained inference and report ambient conditions and throttling observations.
Document Changes Made: Add temperature-versus-time results and discuss thermal limits and whether the platform throttles.

Reviewer Comment: Long-duration stability should be evaluated for memory leakage, thermal throttling, filesystem reliability, and inference drift.
Author Response: We will add a multi-hour or multi-day endurance test, or clearly identify this as a deployment limitation if unavailable.
Document Changes Made: Report duration, reboot behavior, RAM trend, temperature, storage integrity, inference timing, and prediction stability.

Reviewer Comment: The custom PCB should be shown clearly and distinguished from the MangoPi development board.
Author Response: We will clarify which measurements use the MangoPi board and which use the custom PCB.
Document Changes Made: Add clear photographs or diagrams of the custom PCB and revise inconsistent hardware descriptions and figure captions.

Reviewer Comment: Electrical safety, isolation distance, creepage, clearance, surge protection, and relevant smart-meter standards should be discussed before claiming industrial viability.
Author Response: We will moderate industrial-viability language and document the safety design and standards status.
Document Changes Made: Add safety limitations and measured or designed values for isolation, creepage, clearance, protection, enclosure, and applicable standards.

Reviewer Comment: Client-side JWT routing alone does not prevent unauthorized backend access.
Author Response: We will describe and test server-side authentication, authorization, ownership checks, token validation, and role enforcement.
Document Changes Made: Revise the security subsection to remove the implication that client-side routing is a security boundary and report endpoint-authorization tests.

Reviewer Comment: Stripe integration alone does not establish PCI-DSS compliance.
Author Response: We will moderate the compliance claim and describe only the payment-data handling properties actually implemented and assessed.
Document Changes Made: Replace the PCI-DSS assertion with a qualified statement unless a formal compliance assessment is available.

Reviewer Comment: The paper should include failure-mode analysis for connectivity, reboot, model corruption, SPI failure, NAND corruption, power outage, and incorrect predictions.
Author Response: We will add a system failure-mode and recovery analysis covering detection, fallback, recovery, and user or utility notification.
Document Changes Made: Add a failure-mode table and explain which services continue operating under each fault.

Reviewer Comment: Source code, trained models, firmware, quantization scripts, hardware files, and exact dataset splits should be available in a persistent repository.
Author Response: We will create a persistent repository or clearly state which artifacts are available and provide reproducible release versions.
Document Changes Made: Add repository DOI or URL, license, model files, firmware, scripts, PCB files, environment specification, and split manifests to Data Availability.

Reviewer Comment: Several figures contain text that is too small and should be redrawn with consistent notation.
Author Response: We will redraw figures at publication scale with readable fonts, consistent units, labels, and technical notation.
Document Changes Made: Review every figure and table for font size, axis labels, units, legends, and caption consistency.

Reviewer Comment: The manuscript is excessively long and repetitive, especially in generic web-technology and smart-grid motivation sections.
Author Response: We will reduce repetition and retain only material needed to support the edge-NILM and embedded-system contribution.
Document Changes Made: Condense the Introduction, web/mobile/payment sections, repeated result summaries, and generic technology descriptions.

Reviewer Comment: Novelty against existing edge-based NILM systems is unclear and first claims should be supported by a concise technical comparison.
Author Response: We will distinguish system-integration contributions from established algorithmic components and avoid unsupported first claims.
Document Changes Made: Add a comparison table covering hardware, memory, power, model, latency, privacy, datasets, and adaptation; revise novelty language.

Reviewer Comment: Performance improvements over Seq2Point, UNet-NILM, and BERT4NILM lack confidence intervals or significance testing.
Author Response: We will repeat experiments across independent seeds and report variation and statistical tests where comparable baseline implementations are available.
Document Changes Made: Add mean, standard deviation or confidence intervals, number of runs, test units, and statistical-test details to performance tables.

Reviewer Comment: Dataset splitting and cross-dataset evaluation need explicit description, including fine-tuning and dataset-specific optimization.
Author Response: We will provide exact split and adaptation information and revise terminology to match the actual protocol.
Document Changes Made: Add a dataset-protocol matrix and disclose all normalization, threshold, model-selection, and adaptation use of target data.

Reviewer Comment: An ablation study is needed for dilated residual blocks, weighted focal loss, INT8 quantization, and compiler optimization.
Author Response: We will add component-wise ablations under controlled experimental conditions.
Document Changes Made: Add an ablation section and report both accuracy and embedded resource effects for each component.

Reviewer Comment: MAE and F1 alone are insufficient; include precision, recall, SAE, and energy estimation accuracy with justification of metrics.
Author Response: We will define and report a complete NILM metric suite and explain the operational meaning of each metric.
Document Changes Made: Add SAE, normalized error, energy accuracy, per-appliance precision, recall, F1, MAE, RMSE, and threshold definitions.

Reviewer Comment: Privacy is discussed conceptually; residual risks and comparison with federated or encrypted approaches are not evaluated.
Author Response: We will frame local processing as exposure reduction rather than a formal privacy guarantee and add threat scenarios and residual risks.
Document Changes Made: Add a privacy threat model covering raw data, inference outputs, compromised devices, traffic analysis, backend access, federated learning, and encrypted inference.

Reviewer Comment: Scalability to thousands or millions of meters needs discussion of updates, maintenance, model synchronization, and reliability.
Author Response: We will add a deployment-scale discussion grounded in the measured power, bandwidth, storage, and maintenance constraints.
Document Changes Made: Describe provisioning, firmware and model updates, rollback, monitoring, key management, fleet management, and manufacturing reliability.

Reviewer Comment: Harmonic measurements should be validated against a commercial or certified reference analyzer.
Author Response: We will add reference-analyzer validation if available; otherwise we will describe the result as prototype-level THD estimation and remove compliance claims.
Document Changes Made: Report calibration, controlled loads, error, repeatability, FFT settings, analyzer comparison, and the limits of IEEE 519 interpretation.

Reviewer Comment: Inference latency must be aligned with the intended sampling interval and practical real-time operation.

Document Changes Made: Correct the 111-second or 101���123-second values, define the input window, calculate update latency, and revise real-time wo

Reviewer Comment: The paper should discuss long-term robustness under changing household behavior and appliance inventories.

Document Changes Made: Expand the limitations and future-work section with continual evaluation and field-deployment protocols.

Reviewer Comment: Computational complexity analysis is needed, including operations, memory footprint, parameters, and inference efficiency.
Author Response: We will report architecture complexity and hardware-normalized efficiency metrics.
Document Changes Made: Add parameter count, MACs or operations per window, peak activation memory, model size, energy per inference, throughput per watt, and RAM usage.

Reviewer Comment: Implementation details needed for reproduction are missing, including seeds, software versions, repetitions, optimizer settings, schedules, and training hardware.
Author Response: We will provide a complete reproducibility configuration for training, evaluation, quantization, and deployment.
Document Changes Made: Add a reproducibility table and persistent artifact repository with exact splits and environment versions.

Reviewer Comment: Cloud-assisted forecasting needs limitations analysis for connectivity loss, communication delay, and cloud interruption.
Author Response: We will explain the effect of connectivity and define local fallback behavior or state that forecasting is unavailable during cloud outages.
Document Changes Made: Add cloud dependency, communication-latency measurements, retry and buffering behavior, outage fallback, and forecasting-scope limitations.

Reviewer Comment: Hardware efficiency should use standardized metrics such as energy per inference and throughput per watt, not only power and cost.
Author Response: We will add standardized efficiency metrics and clearly define workload and peripheral conditions.
Document Changes Made: Extend hardware tables with energy per inference, samples or seconds processed per watt, throughput per watt, model size, and equivalent-workload notes.

Reviewer Comment: The limitations and future-work section should cover three-phase systems, industrial environments, larger appliance sets, grid standards, cybersecurity, and long-term field validation.
